verdict.rationale: ROS 2's official docs include a tutorial on launching a simulation with Gazebo and ROS 2, and a long-time user notes ROS gives you simulation 'for free' if you follow its conventions. The simulator itself is Gazebo, a separate tool, so the capability depends on that integration rather than on ROS 2 alone. Missing for 10: any evidence of realistic physics engines or sensor models, documentation beyond a tutorial title, and hands-on reports of simulation fidelity before hardware.
